mainTopic: Mixtures in רבי אליעזר's rulings: mixed blood needing different placements, mixed cups of fit and unfit blood, and plain water mixed into purification water.
overview: The amud opens with a משנה about blood from two קרבנות that got mixed together. If both need the same number of placements, the כהן simply does that number. If one needs four placements and the other needs one, רבי אליעזר says to do four and רבי יהושע says to do one. They argue over בל תוסיף and בל תגרע, and רבי יהושע finally argues that adding is an active wrong while leaving out is passive. The גמרא then turns to cups of blood from blemished animals that were mixed with fit cups. רבי אלעזר says רבי אליעזר allowed the remaining cups only two at a time, and he reads the משנה's 'one' as 'one pair.' The גמרא explains why the משנה needed to teach the argument about both limbs and blood. Next it quotes a משנה from פרה about plain water that fell into a flask of purification water. It works out which rules רבי אליעזר must hold so that his advice of two sprinklings makes sense. ריש לקיש, רבא and רב אשי each give a different explanation. The amud ends with a ברייתא from רבי that seems to contradict ריש לקיש, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Mixing blood that needs the same number of placements
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with the easy cases. If both bloods need one placement, the כהן does one. If both need four, he does four.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood that needs one placement got mixed with other blood that also needs one placement, the כהן puts it on the מזבח once. If blood that needs four placements got mixed with other blood that needs four, he puts it on four times.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out the simple cases of mixed blood, where both קרבנות need the same number of placements on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both kinds of blood need the same treatment, the mixture does not create any problem. Doing the shared number of placements fulfills the מצוה for both קרבנות. These easy cases set up the hard case in the next step, where the numbers do not match.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'placement': putting blood on the מזבח
A single placement of blood (for example, a בכור or מעשר)
Four placements, one on each corner of the מזבח (for example, a חטאת)
Got mixed together

phrases.english: Blood that is placed with one placement
that got mixed with blood that is placed with one placement
shall be placed with one placement.
(Of them,) blood needing four placements mixed with blood needing four placements
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: shall be placed with four placements.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנִּיתָּנִין בְּמַתָּנָה אַחַת שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בַּנִּיתָּנִין בְּמַתָּנָה אַחַת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When mixed bloods need the same number of placements, the כהן does that number.

steps.title: Four placements mixed with one placement: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: When blood needing four placements mixes with blood needing one, רבי אליעזר says to do four and רבי יהושע says to do one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood needing four placements got mixed with blood needing one placement, רבי אליעזר says to do four placements, and רבי יהושע says to do one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the hard case, where the two bloods need different numbers of placements, and two תנאים disagree about what to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither answer fits both קרבנות perfectly. Four is too many for the one-placement blood, and one is too few for the four-placement blood. רבי אליעזר picks the larger number and רבי יהושע picks the smaller one. The next steps explain why.
steps.whatToRemember: Four mixed with one: רבי אליעזר says four, רבי יהושע says one.

phrases.english: Blood needing four placements mixed with blood needing one placement

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יִנָּתְנוּ בְּמַתַּן אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it shall be placed with four placements,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יִנָּתְנוּ בְּמַתָּנָה אֶחָת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: it shall be placed with one placement.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתַּן אַרְבַּע בְּמַתָּנָה אַחַת – רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the easy cases to the case where the numbers of placements do not match.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: four placements; רבי יהושע: one placement.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: doing one placement means taking away
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר challenges רבי יהושע: if you do only one placement, you break בל תגרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: With one placement, the כהן is breaking the rule of 'do not take away'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר attacks רבי יהושע's view. Doing only one placement shortchanges the blood that needs four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids adding to or taking away from a מצוה. The four-placement blood is getting only one placement, so three are missing. That looks like taking away, which is בל תגרע.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not take away': the prohibition against doing less of a מצוה than required
Breaks or violates (a prohibition)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תִּגְרַע!
phrases.english: But he is breaking 'do not take away'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תִּגְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהושע's ruling from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling to do one placement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The four-placement blood gets less than it needs, which breaks בל תגרע.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: doing four placements means adding
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע hits back: if you do four placements, you break בל תוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: With four placements, the כהן is breaking the rule of 'do not add'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers with a matching challenge against רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one-placement blood is getting three extra placements. That looks like adding to the מצוה, which is בל תוסיף. Now both sides seem to break a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not add': the prohibition against doing more of a מצוה than required

steps.confusionAlert: Both בל תוסיף and בל תגרע come from the same פסוק. At this point each option seems to break one of them. In step 5, רבי אליעזר argues that his option escapes the problem, and only in step 7 does רבי יהושע argue that one problem is worse than the other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תּוֹסִיף!
phrases.english: But he is breaking 'do not add'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תּוֹסִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge that mirrors רבי אליעזר's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling to do four placements
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The one-placement blood gets more than it needs, which breaks בל תוסיף.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: adding only counts when the blood is alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר defends his view: בל תוסיף applies only when the blood is by itself, not when it is part of a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: 'Do not add' was said only when the blood is by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's challenge by limiting when בל תוסיף applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His claim is that adding is forbidden only when someone puts extra placements on blood that stands alone. In a mixture, the extra placements are really meant for the other blood, so this is not 'adding.' That removes the problem with his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: When it is by itself, not mixed with anything
It was said only for ...

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
'Do not add' was not stated
except when it is by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: לֹא נֶאֱמַר בַּל תּוֹסִיף אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's counter-challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Doing four placements on a mixture breaks בל תוסיף.
steps.terutzMaskana: בל תוסיף applies only to blood that is alone, so a mixture is not a problem.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the same logic works for taking away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע turns the argument around: if the rule about being alone limits בל תוסיף, it also limits בל תגרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: 'Do not take away' was also said only when the blood is by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע shows that רבי אליעזר's answer helps both sides equally, so it cannot decide the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mixture is exempt from בל תוסיף, then by the same reasoning it is exempt from בל תגרע. That cancels רבי אליעזר's original challenge from step 3. The two sides are now even again.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
'Do not take away' was not stated
except when it is by itself!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לֹא נֶאֱמַר בַּל תִּגְרַע אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אליעזר's own reasoning to cancel his challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אליעזר's claim that his answer gives his view an advantage
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'when it is by itself' limit applies equally to both prohibitions.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: adding is an action, taking away is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע gives another argument: adding placements is an active violation, while leaving them out is passive, so doing one placement is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע also said: When you place four, you break 'do not add' and you do it with an action. When you don't place them, you break 'do not take away,' but you did not do any action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives an extra argument that tips the balance toward his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if both options involve a prohibition, they are not equal. Extra placements mean actively doing something wrong. Leaving placements out is only failing to act. A passive violation is less serious than an active one, so one placement is the better choice.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; brings an extra argument
An action done with your hand; an active deed
Sitting and not acting; a passive approach (the idea behind this step)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's main point is that a passive violation (not placing) is better than an active one (placing extra). That is why he rules to do one placement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic idea that when every option involves a problem, not acting is better than acting wrongly.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua also said:
When you placed, you broke 'do not add,'
and you did an action with your hand.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁלֹּא נָתַתָּ – עָבַרְתָּ עַל בַּל תִּגְרַע,
phrases.english: When you did not place, you broke 'do not take away,'
but you did not do an action with your hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כְּשֶׁנָּתַתָּ – עָבַרְתָּ עַל בַּל תּוֹסִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After making the two sides even, רבי יהושע adds a reason that favors his view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's ruling to do one placement
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that an active violation is worse than a passive one.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits רבי אליעזר's leniency to pairs of cups
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that רבי אליעזר allowed the remaining cups of blood to be offered only two at a time, not one at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: רבי אליעזר allowed the cups only two by two, but not one by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a statement from רבי אלעזר that narrows how far רבי אליעזר's leniency in the משנה goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, some cups hold blood from blemished animals, which may not be offered. רבי אליעזר says that after one cup is offered, the rest may be offered too. רבי אלעזר explains that this works only two at a time, because then at least one cup in each pair is surely good. If you offer one cup alone, it might be the bad one.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Declared fit, allowed it to be used
Two at a time
One at a time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two names. רבי אֶלְעָזָר is the later אמורא who is speaking here. רבי אֱלִיעֶזֶר is the תנא from the משנה whose opinion is being explained.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Elazar says:
Rabbi Eliezer did not permit [the remaining cups]
except two by two,
but one by one, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֶלָּא שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of a new case in the משנה (mixed cups of blood), separate from the debate about placements in steps 3-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the remaining mixed cups may be offered only in pairs, never one cup alone.

steps.title: רב דימי challenges from the words of the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי quotes the חכמים: even if all the cups except one were offered, that last one is poured out. This suggests רבי אליעזר would allow even a single last cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי objects: And the Rabbis say, even if all of them were offered except one of them, it is poured into the drain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי challenges רבי אלעזר from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say that even when only one cup is left, it must be poured out. That sounds like a reply to רבי אליעזר, so it implies that רבי אליעזר allows even one single cup to be offered. That goes against רבי אלעזר's rule that cups may only be offered two at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: It is poured into the drain channel in the Temple courtyard
Drain channel

phrases.english: Rav Dimi raises an objection:
And the Rabbis say:
Even if all of them were offered
except for one of them,
it shall be poured into the drain.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אלעזר's limit from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that רבי אליעזר did not allow cups to be offered one at a time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים argue about a single last cup, so רבי אליעזר must allow that single cup to be offered.

steps.title: "One" means one pair
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב explains that 'one' in the משנה means one pair of cups, so רבי אלעזר's rule still holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said to רבי ירמיה בר תחליפא: I will explain it to you. What is 'one'? One pair.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב answers רב דימי's challenge by reading the word 'one' in the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's 'except for one of them' means one pair of cups, not one single cup. So the argument is about a last pair, which fits רבי אלעזר's rule that even רבי אליעזר never allows a single cup alone.

keyTerms.meaning: I will explain it to you
A pair

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, even רבי אליעזר allows the mixed cups only in pairs. The משנה's word 'one' means 'one pair.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov said to him,
to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Tachlifa:
I will explain it to you:
What is "one"? One pair.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ: מַאי אֶחָד – זוּג אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב דימי's challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One' means a single cup, so רבי אליעזר allows a single cup.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One' means one pair, so רבי אליעזר never allows a single cup alone.

steps.title: Why the argument is needed for limbs and for blood: the first side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that if the argument were taught only about limbs, we might think רבי אליעזר is lenient only there, since the atonement was already done, and that he agrees with the חכמים about blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary. For if it were stated only in that case, I would say רבי אליעזר said it in that case because its atonement was already done. But in this case, say he agrees with the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why the משנה had to teach the same argument twice, once about limbs and once about cups of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With limbs, the blood was already offered, so the atonement is complete and burning the limbs is less critical. That might be why רבי אליעזר is lenient there. With blood, the atonement itself is at stake, so we might think he agrees with the חכמים. So the משנה had to teach the blood case too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; the גמרא explains why each case had to be taught
Atonement, which comes through offering the blood
I might say, one might think
Agrees

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if it were stated in that case,
phrases.notes: 'That case' is the earlier argument in the משנה about mixed limbs.

phrases.english: [I would say] it is in that case that Rabbi Eliezer says [they are fit],
because its atonement was already done;
but in this case [of the cups],
say that he agrees with the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא; דְּאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: why the משנה repeats the same argument in two cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching the argument only about limbs would leave room to think רבי אליעזר agrees with the חכמים about blood.

steps.title: The second side: both cases had to be taught
steps.stepSummary: If the argument were taught only about blood, we might think the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about limbs. So both cases are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were stated only in this case, I would say the Rabbis said it in this case, but in that case, say they agree with רבי אליעזר. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation by showing the other side and concludes that the משנה needed both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים might be strict only about blood, where the atonement depends on it. About limbs, after the atonement is done, they might agree with רבי אליעזר. Since each case alone could mislead us, the משנה teaches both.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority view (the same as חכמים)
They agree

steps.whatToRemember: The argument appears twice so we know both sides keep their views in both cases: רבי אליעזר is lenient even with blood, and the חכמים are strict even with limbs.

phrases.english: And if it were stated in this case [of the cups],
[I would say] it is in this case that the Rabbis say [they are unfit],
but in that case [of the limbs],
say that they agree with Rabbi Eliezer;
[therefore] it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא – בְּהָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation begun in step 11 by giving the other side.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה must teach the argument about both limbs and blood. Otherwise we might think רבי אליעזר agrees about blood, or that the חכמים agree about limbs.

steps.title: A related case: plain water falls into a flask of purification water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in which רבי אליעזר allows two sprinklings from a mixed flask, while the חכמים disqualify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in another משנה: if any amount of plain water fell into a flask of purification water, רבי אליעזר says the כהן should sprinkle two times, and the חכמים say the water is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה from a different מסכת that shows the same kind of argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the mixing is between purification water and plain water, not blood or limbs. רבי אליעזר again looks for a way to save the mixture, this time by sprinkling twice. The חכמים do not allow the mixture at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A small flask
A sprinkling of purification water on an impure person
They disqualify it

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פרה 9:1.

phrases.english: A flask into which there fell
phrases.notes: The flask holds the special purification water made with the ashes of the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: any amount of water –
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He should sprinkle two sprinklings,
but the Sages disqualify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about a mixture, from מסכת פרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: sprinkle twice from the mixed flask. חכמים: the mixture is disqualified.

steps.title: The Rabbis' view is easy to explain
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold three rules: mixing spreads everywhere, a sprinkling needs a minimum amount, and two sprinklings do not join together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense why the חכמים disqualify the water. They hold that the waters are fully blended, that each sprinkling needs a minimum amount of purification water, and that two sprinklings cannot be added together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חכמים first, because their view is simple. This sets up the harder question: what does רבי אליעזר hold?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of בילה, every drop has some plain water in it, so no single sprinkling has a full שיעור of purification water. Because sprinklings do not join, sprinkling twice does not help. So the person cannot become pure with this water.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (the hard part comes next)
There is mixing: every drop holds some of each liquid
A minimum required amount
They combine or add up together

phrases.english: Granted, the Rabbis –
they hold there is mixing,
phrases.notes: He means the two waters blend completely, so every drop has a little plain water in it.

phrases.english: and a sprinkling requires a minimum measure,
and sprinklings do not combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the חכמים' side of the משנה just quoted, preparing a contrast with רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים hold יש בילה, הזאה צריכה שיעור, and אין מצטרפין להזאות.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר hold? He must hold there is mixing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי אליעזר's reasoning and shows he cannot hold there is no mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what does רבי אליעזר hold? If he holds the waters do not blend, then sprinkling twice proves nothing, because maybe both times only plain water came out. So he must hold that there is mixing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins checking each of the three rules to see which ones רבי אליעזר could hold. It starts with בילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there were no blending, a given drop could be pure plain water, and two sprinklings could both miss the purification water. That would make his advice of two sprinklings pointless, so he must agree that יש בילה.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he hold?
There is no mixing: the liquids stay separate
Perhaps

phrases.english: But Rabbi Eliezer –
what does he hold?
If he holds there is no mixing,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מַזֶּה שְׁתֵּי הַזָּאוֹת מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: when he sprinkles two sprinklings, what of it?
Perhaps both times he is sprinkling plain water!
Rather, he holds there is mixing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַאי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the חכמים, turns to the harder side: רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three rules (בילה, שיעור, combining) does רבי אליעזר hold?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first one is settled: he must hold יש בילה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר must hold a sprinkling needs a minimum amount
steps.stepSummary: If no minimum were needed, one sprinkling would be enough, so רבי אליעזר must hold a שיעור is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds a sprinkling does not need a minimum amount, why would two sprinklings be needed? One would do. So he must hold a sprinkling needs a minimum amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the second rule, about the minimum amount, and settles it the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we already know he holds יש בילה, every drop has some purification water. If any tiny amount were enough, one sprinkling would work, so asking for two shows he requires a שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?
A sprinkling needs a minimum amount of purification water

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר אֵין הַזָּאָה צְרִיכָה שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: If he holds a sprinkling does not require a minimum measure,
why do I need two sprinklings?
Rather, he holds a sprinkling requires a minimum measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קָסָבַר אֵין הַזָּאָה צְרִיכָה שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the step-by-step check, moving from בילה to שיעור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אליעזר require a minimum amount for a sprinkling?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, otherwise one sprinkling would be enough.

steps.title: Either way, two sprinklings still do not seem to work
steps.stepSummary: Whether sprinklings combine or not, there seems to be no reason two sprinklings should work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds sprinklings do not add up, what good are two sprinklings? And even if they do add up, who says the two together reach the minimum amount of purification water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last rule and finds that both options cause a problem. Now רבי אליעזר's view seems impossible to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sprinklings cannot combine, each one alone is short of the שיעור, so two do not help. If they can combine, we still do not know how much plain water fell in, so even two might not hold enough purification water.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What does it help?
Who says?
That the minimum amount is filled up

phrases.english: And if he holds sprinklings do not combine,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מַזֶּה שְׁתֵּי הַזָּאוֹת מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: when he sprinkles two sprinklings, what of it?
And even if sprinklings do combine,
who says it fills up the measure for him?
phrases.notes: Only an unknown amount of plain water fell in, so maybe most of what he sprinkles is plain water.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי קָסָבַר אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין לְהַזָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing two rules, the third rule leaves no workable option, so the question becomes a real challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that two sprinklings are enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: if sprinklings cannot combine, two do not help. If they can combine, there is still no guarantee that two reach the שיעור of purification water.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the case is a half-and-half mixture
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says רבי אליעזר does hold יש בילה and needs a שיעור, but the משנה is talking about a mixture of equal amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: really, there is mixing and a sprinkling needs a minimum amount. The case here is where equal amounts of the two waters were mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the problem by narrowing the case in the משנה. This explains why two sprinklings work for רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that we did not know how much plain water fell in. If the mixture is exactly half and half, two sprinklings together hold one full sprinkling's worth of purification water. So the worry of 'who says it reaches the שיעור' goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeping the earlier assumption)
What case are we dealing with here?
One in one: equal amounts

steps.whatToRemember: For ריש לקיש, רבי אליעזר holds יש בילה and that a sprinkling needs a שיעור. Two sprinklings work only because the mixture was half and half.
steps.confusionAlert: The words כל שהו in the משנה seem to mean a tiny amount of plain water. ריש לקיש reads the case as an equal mixture, and that is exactly what makes two sprinklings enough.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Actually, there is mixing,
and a sprinkling requires a minimum measure;
and here, what are we dealing with?
A case where they were mixed one in one.
phrases.notes: Half plain water and half purification water, so two sprinklings together hold one sprinkling's worth of purification water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְעוֹלָם יֵשׁ בִּילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma by limiting the משנה to an equal mixture.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to talk about an unknown amount of plain water, so two sprinklings might not reach the שיעור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mixture is one to one, so two sprinklings together surely hold a full שיעור of purification water.

steps.title: רבא: The Second Sprinkling Is a Penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי אליעזר holds יש בילה and that a הזאה needs no שיעור. One sprinkling should really be enough, but the רבנן required two as a penalty, so that a person who mixes the water does not gain from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, there is mixing, and a sprinkling does not need a minimum amount. The Rabbis made a penalty so that he would not gain from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different answer to the question of step 17: why two sprinklings are needed. He says one is really enough, and the second is only a penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said רבי אליעזר needs a שיעור. רבא disagrees and says no שיעור is needed, so by the basic law one sprinkling would work because the fit water is spread everywhere. The demand for a second sprinkling is a קנס from the רבנן, so that someone who waters down the precious מי חטאת does not profit from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Used to keep an earlier idea while changing a different detail.
Mixing: the idea that a mixture spreads evenly through all its parts.
A minimum required amount
A penalty decreed by the רבנן
He will gain or benefit

phrases.english: Rava said: Really, there is mixing,
and a sprinkling does not need a minimum amount;
and it is a penalty the Rabbis imposed,
so that he should not gain from it.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the one in square brackets. Both mean 'gain'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם יֵשׁ בִּילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from ריש לקיש's to the difficulty of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic penalty: the basic law says one sprinkling is enough, but the רבנן added a second
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two sprinklings must be needed by the basic law, which seemed to make no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: By the basic law one sprinkling works, since there is mixing and no שיעור. The second sprinkling is a קנס.

steps.title: רב אשי: No Mixing, So Sprinkle Twice
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה, so the כהן sprinkles two sprinklings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There is no mixing; he should sprinkle two sprinklings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third answer. He says רבי אליעזר holds that the mixture does not spread evenly, so the כהן does two sprinklings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש and רבא both said רבי אליעזר holds יש בילה. רב אשי goes the other way and says אין בילה. Since the fit water is not spread evenly, one sprinkling might contain no fit water at all, so the כהן sprinkles twice.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no mixing: a mixture does not spread evenly through all its parts.
He should sprinkle
Sprinklings

steps.confusionAlert: Back in step 15 the גמרא showed that רבי אליעזר cannot hold אין בילה. רב אשי goes back to the very view the גמרא pushed away, so read his answer as a fresh approach. It is not a continuation of ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: There is no mixing;
he should sprinkle two sprinklings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֵין בִּילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation that rejects the יש בילה starting point used by ריש לקיש and רבא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the basic assumption from יש בילה to אין בילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר must hold יש בילה, as step 15 argued
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר holds אין בילה. Because one sprinkling might have no fit water, two sprinklings are done.

steps.title: A ברייתא: For רבי אליעזר, Any Amount Purifies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא. רבי says that according to רבי אליעזר, a sprinkling of any amount purifies, a sprinkling needs no שיעור, and even a sprinkling that is half fit and half unfit works.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבי says: According to רבי אליעזר, a sprinkling of any amount purifies; a sprinkling does not need a minimum amount; a sprinkling that is half fit and half unfit works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack ריש לקיש. He said רבי אליעזר needs a שיעור for a sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's answer in step 18 depends on רבי אליעזר requiring a minimum amount. רבי's ברייתא says clearly that, for רבי אליעזר, הזאה אין צריכה שיעור and כל שהוא purifies. It even says a half-and-half sprinkling works. That seems to contradict ריש לקיש directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even a tiny one
Half fit and half unfit

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא seems to match רבא's view (no שיעור needed), but it clashes with ריש לקיש. So it is a real test of ריש לקיש's answer.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rebbi says:
phrases.notes: This challenge is aimed at ריש לקיש, who said רבי אליעזר needs a minimum amount.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Eliezer —
a sprinkling of any amount purifies;
a sprinkling does not need a minimum amount;
a sprinkling that is half fit and half unfit works.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא and רב אשי and goes back to challenge ריש לקיש's answer from step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that רבי אליעזר requires a שיעור for a sprinkling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא from רבי says outright that, for רבי אליעזר, a sprinkling needs no שיעור and any amount purifies. This contradicts ריש לקיש.
